content:
I have a proof in which I'd prefer to leave several lines in the form simp [h2, h5] at h1, because using simp only pulls in a large list of other things.

I see that the linter hates this. Not only do the simp lines get underlined in yellow, anything that touches a hypothesis or goal that has been simped in this way gets tainted and underlined in blue.

There's a helpful tooltip noting that I can set a linter option to ignore the use of flexible tactics. I take it this is considered unwise by default. What are the downsides?

One reason is proof stability. Let's say your proof worked as follows:

simp [...] at ...
exact h

Now assume that some upstream code adds a new @[simp] theorem which allows simp to prove what we just proved by exact h. Then the proof above already completes at the simp [...] at ... step, so the subsequent exact h produces an error. If you instead use simp only this problem cannot occur.

Note that it's still fine to use simp (without only) as a terminal tactic, that is the final tactic in a branch of a proof. In this case, simp getting "stronger" does not cause any problems.

In the very same proof I have the line have h02 := h01.commutative.comm, which is invalid in current Mathlib. (My installation is some months old.) So proof stability is already shot; it's not like my proof will become stable if I follow the linter's advice.

(h01 is docs#IsCyclic ; IsCyclic.commutative currently exists but is deprecated. However, IsCyclic.commutative.comm does not exist; IsCyclic.commutative used to have type Std.Commutative _ but now has type IsMulCommutative _.)

Stability isn't boolean, a specific breakage doesn't invalidate the reasons to prefer simp only
(btw I believe I broke your proof, sorry for the trouble!)

Michael said:

I have a proof in which I'd prefer to leave several lines in the form simp [h2, h5] at h1, because using simp only pulls in a large list of other things.

Maybe have h1' : <what you want h1 to change into> := by simpa [h2, h5] using h1 will work for you. This is better than simp? if simp? is pulling in a large list and if what you want to change h1 into is relatively short.

Michael said:

In the very same proof I have the line have h02 := h01.commutative.comm, which is invalid in current Mathlib. (My installation is some months old.) So proof stability is already shot; it's not like my proof will become stable if I follow the linter's advice.

From a pragmatic perspective, a missing identifier is much easier to fix than a simp call that suddenly got stronger.

One other perspective on this is that whoever is deleting a public declaration in Mathlib knows they are making a backwards incompatible design and is responsible for fixing all upstream declarations in Mathlib. But a non-terminal simp is unique in that if a library contains non-terminal simps, then adding simp lemmas to mathlib is now a backwards incompatible change. This places a larger burden on contributors, because now everyone who adds lemmas needs to be responsible for fixing downstream proofs.
Renaming an identifier in mathlib also comes with a deprecation warning: the old code will still work for several months, but warn you about the change.
